questions.q: What does transformation_ctx="raw_orders" enable on the source read?
options: Job bookmarking, so a re-run only processes new records instead of reprocessing everything
Automatic encryption of the raw data at rest
A faster network connection to S3
Automatic deletion of the raw source table after the job runs
questions.explain: The transformation_ctx is what lets Glue's job bookmark track, per source, which records have already been processed.

questions.q: Why is unit_price cast to decimal(10,2) instead of left as a plain float or string?
options: A fixed-precision decimal keeps money math exact instead of relying on imprecise floating-point values
Decimal types are required for Spark to read a column at all
It has no real effect; any numeric type would behave identically
Decimal values take up less storage than integers
questions.explain: Casting price to a fixed-precision decimal avoids the rounding and representation issues that come with floating-point arithmetic on money values.

questions.q: Where is order_total computed, and why does that matter?
options: Inside the ETL job itself, so every downstream report uses the identical formula
In each individual Athena query that needs it
It is not computed anywhere in this pipeline
In the Redshift COPY command's WHERE clause
questions.explain: order_total doesn't exist upstream — computing it once inside northfield-orders-etl guarantees Finance's and Ops's reports both use the exact same formula.

questions.q: Why do dropDuplicates and the null-key filter belong inside the ETL job rather than left for each report to handle separately?
options: Because this is the one place everyone's reports ultimately flow through, instead of each consumer discovering and patching the same issue independently
Because Spark cannot write Parquet files containing duplicate rows
Because Redshift's COPY command automatically rejects any duplicate rows on its own
They don't matter; leaving them out would have no effect on the data
questions.explain: Centralizing dedup and null-filtering in the one shared transformation step keeps every downstream consumer's numbers consistent, rather than relying on each one to catch the same problem.

questions.q: What does enableUpdateCatalog=True do for this job's sink?
options: Automatically registers the written curated output as a Glue Data Catalog table, with no separate crawler needed
Automatically deletes old partitions from the curated zone
Enables encryption on the Redshift COPY step
Schedules the job to run nightly without EventBridge
questions.explain: enableUpdateCatalog registers the curated Parquet output as northfield_catalog.northfield_orders_curated automatically, without running a separate crawler on the curated side.
